caption: The drawing features a rectangular piece of fabric with a checkered pattern, oriented horizontally on a plain, off-white background. The fabric is composed of alternating red and white squares arranged in a grid, resembling a classic gingham or checkerboard pattern. The edges of the fabric are slightly wavy, and the overall shape is not perfectly rectangular, with slight irregularities suggesting it is either draped or loosely laid out. Within the checkered pattern, two specific white areas stand out: one on the left side, near the bottom, and another on the right side, roughly in the middle, both breaking the regularity of the pattern. The drawing is bordered by a faint rectangular outline, framing the fabric within the larger blank space of the background. There is a small, faint inscription on the bottom left that reads "PATTERN ACTUAL SIZE," and another inscription on the bottom right corner with the name "FRANK MABER."
title: Wool Tablecloth
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
